content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a yeasted dough snack commonly served in school lunches. They have a golden crust, a lightly salty flavor, and a soft, chewy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional soft pretzels are made from wheat flour, water, yeast, and a pinch of salt.
The iconic knot shape dates back to medieval Europe and originally symbolized crossed hands in prayer.
In the United States they are often served with mustard or cheese dip.
In school cafeterias they provide a quick source of carbohydrates and energy for children.
Whole‑grain versions add extra fiber while keeping the classic taste.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Soft pretzels supply easily digestible carbs that give energy for learning and physical activity.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough provides small amounts of B1, B2 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Wheat flour contributes iron, supporting normal blood formation.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, soft pretzels are typically baked without large amounts of added oil, making them less calorie‑dense.

items.title: Fiber (in whole‑grain version)
items.content: Whole‑grain pretzels are richer in dietary fiber, which aids healthy digestion.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapidly absorbed carbs can cause a quick blood‑sugar spike, especially in children prone to diabetes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The salty flavor comes from added salt, which may be a concern if sodium intake is excessive.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pretzels contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some children may experience allergic reactions to wheat flour.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soft pretzels can be enjoyed plain, split and spread with cream cheese, hummus, or mustard. They also make a good base for sandwiches with ham, cheese, and vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep soft pretzels in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them and reheat in the oven before serving.
